exposure: Category I cesarean section performed in the delivery room
Category I cesarean section performed in the operating room
outcome: Blood routine parameters (e.g., white blood cell counts)
cohort: The study included 126 singleton pregnant women who underwent inpatient delivery at the Second People's Hospital of Nanning between January 2021 and May 2024, undergoing category I cesarean section.
finding: While the decision-to-delivery interval was significantly shorter in the delivery room group, this group also exhibited increased risks including longer surgical durations, higher blood loss, prolonged postoperative antibiotic usage, extended hospital stays, and elevated white blood cell counts, though no notable variations were observed in adverse neonatal outcomes or postoperative fever rates.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean sections performed in the delivery room had a shorter decision-to-delivery interval but were associated with higher maternal risks (e.g., blood loss, longer hospital stays, infection markers) compared to those performed in the operating room, without differing in overall maternal and neonatal outcome indicators like adverse neonatal outcomes.
